title_original: Paris Photo 2026 : Main Sector & Prismes Projects
excerpt_original: At the heart of the nave, the Main sector welcomes newcomers and galleries that are regulars, notably Bienvenu Steinberg & Co (New York), Lia […] Cet article Paris Photo 2026 : Main Sector & Prismes Projects est apparu en premier sur The Eye of Photography Magazine .

blocks.text: At the heart of the nave, the Main sector welcomes newcomers and galleries that are regulars, notably Bienvenu Steinberg & Co (New York), Lia Rumma (Milan), La Cometa (Bogotá), Proyectos Monclova (Mexico City), Silverlens (Manila) and L’Atelier 21 (Casablanca).

Several galleries specializing in historical photography are spread across the Main sector, including Hans P. Kraus Jr., Bruno Tartarin, Gilles Peyroulet, Lunn, Barnabé Moinard and Serge Plantureux. MEM presents a project devoted to Subjective Photography in Japan. Large Glass brings together in Echoes works by Mario Cresci, John Gossage, Guido Guidi, Mark Ruwedel and Ursula Schulz-Dornburg, placed in relation to historical references in photography.

The 44 solo shows allow works and bodies of work to be explored in depth: historical series such as Dirty Windows by Merry Alpern, presented by Miranda gallery; the photographs made by Stanley Kubrick in the 1950s, presented by Duncan Miller; several emblematic series by Kati Horna from Proyectos Monclova; or La Cometa, which presents a series by Miguel Angel Rojas devoted to clandestine encounters in Bogotá’s movie theaters in the 1970s.

Contemporary work is also on view: Bienvenu Steinberg & Co with Juan Manuel Echavarría and his work on the traces of the armed conflict in Colombia, Elle Pérez, a leading figure in New York contemporary photography, with Public Relations gallery, Nadine Ijewere at Huxley-Parlour and Alejandro Cartagena at Patricia Conde. The eleven duo shows notably pair Ion Grigorescu and B. Wurtz at Gregor Podnar (Berlin), Jo Ann Callis and Tania Franco Klein at ROSEGALLERY (Santa Monica), and Kusukazu Uraguchi and Laure Winants at Écho 119 (Paris).

At the entrance to the fair, five galleries join forces around a presentation of Thomas Ruff. Christophe Gaillard presents an installation by SMITH, while Klemm’s, by exhibiting a project by Viktoria Binschtok, creates a link between the Main sector and the Digital sector.
* Some projects are presented jointly by several galleries.
Paris Photo Nov. 12–15, 2026 | Grand Palais 1 pm – 8 pm (Sunday 7 pm) Avenue Winston Churchill 75008, Paris, France Booth P01 www.parisphoto.com
